newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The national radio will hold two separate talk-shows for the two contenders in this week's run-off presidential election, incumbent President Ion Iliescu and the opposition leader Emil Constantinescu.
The two are to answer questions from the radio audience.

* Health Minister Daniela Bartos announced she had ordered a residency exam for 3,000 medical graduates to be canceled due to massive fraud, with some 800 candidates knowing the subjects in advance. The exam was rescheduled for January.
* Iliescu met representatives of major trade unions countrywide to answer questions on his commitment to reform and improving living standards.

He said he was willing to support the government formed by the Democratic Convention (CDR) and the Social Democratic Union (USD) provided that their platform would fulfil their electoral promises and not stir social unrest.
Iliescu said the president should not have the same political affiliation as the ruling coalition in order to preserve national stability.

* The new parliament majority formed by the CDR and USD after the November 3 elections is a stable majority that will enact reform laws to win the approval of deputies, a National Peasant Party (PNTCD) representative told a news conference.
* Iliescu's negative electoral speeches can in no way guarantee the social stability he preaches, PNTCD secretary general Radu Vasile said.

* Siderca SA steel mill in the southern town of Calarasi, on the Danube river, offered three-year bonds with a face value of 20,000 lei and a 57 percent annual interest rate. Siderca is the first state-owned company to issue bonds.
Siderca sources said many individuals and firms bought bonds on Monday.
